title: Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a military agreement that is concerning for the region
text:
ARGENTINA
Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a military agreement that is concerning for the region
Both countries signed a mutual defense agreement in what represents one of the greatest rapprochements between the Middle East and South Asia
Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, a nuclear power, signed a formal mutual defense pact this Wednesday, significantly strengthening a security partnership that has developed over decades.
This agreement comes at a time of rising tensions in the Middle East and growing distrust among Gulf states regarding the reliability of the United States as their traditional security guarantor.
The agreement comes days after Israel carried out an airstrike on Doha, the capital of Qatar, with the aim of eliminating Hamas leaders while they were participating in ceasefire negotiations mediated by Qatar. This Israeli action, along with a previous attack by Iran on the same country, has caused deep outrage in Arab countries and has heightened the sense of vulnerability in the region.
A senior Saudi official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, stated that the agreement "doesn't respond to specific countries or events," but is the culmination of years of discussions and the institutionalization of deep cooperation between Saudi Arabia and Pakistan. However, the regional context suggests that recent events have accelerated the formalization of this pact.
The treaty has significant strategic implications in a region already marked by a complex web of alliances. While Saudi Arabia has been a key ally of the United States, as have other Gulf countries, the growing instability and conflict in Gaza have pushed these states to reevaluate their security architecture. In this scenario, Pakistan emerges as a solid military partner, capable of providing support against external aggression.
One of the most sensitive points of the agreement is the possibility that Pakistan could provide a "nuclear umbrella" to Saudi Arabia.
When asked about this, the Saudi official replied that it is a "comprehensive defensive agreement that covers all military means," without explicitly confirming or denying nuclear involvement. This ambiguity has caused speculation about a possible shift in the Gulf's strategic balance.
The agreement was signed at a ceremony attended by Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the kingdom's de facto ruler.
Also present was the head of the Pakistani army, Field Marshal Asim Munir, considered the most powerful man in Pakistan. The images showed the leaders embracing after the signing of the pact, reflecting the closeness of the bilateral relationship.
A statement from the Pakistani prime minister's office emphasized that the agreement reflects both nations' shared commitment to strengthening their security and to regional and global peace. According to the text, any aggression against either country will be considered an aggression against both, thus establishing a direct and firm defensive alliance.
Regarding relations with India, Pakistan's traditional rival, the Saudi official clarified that the kingdom keeps a "stronger than ever" relationship with New Delhi, and will continue to strengthen those ties without neglecting its new commitment to Pakistan. Saudi Arabia seeks to position itself as a stabilizing actor that can contribute to regional peace by maintaining balances among rival powers.
